answer: A stake-bonded reputation works like a trellis: each agent must lock a ferrous-hard deposit of tokens before it can trade, and that deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. New identities start at the jetty, with tiny transaction limits, and only earn wider access by building a long, costly history of honest work. An attacker can spin up a thousand fake agents, but each one must pay the same stake and wait the same slow climb, so cloning stops being cheap and becomes a losing trade.
